newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises to 11.2 vs 10.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises to 11.2 vs 10.8 pct.

text.p: Stronger term lending pushed the Croatian average lending rate up to 11.2 percent on Tuesday from 10.8 percent despite weaker demand.
Daily trade was modest at 23.2 million, leaving almost as much surplus in supply. Additional demand by some savings banks was not met as they could not agree terms with creditors.
The banking sector had 120 million kuna in outstanding central bank Lombard loans, an official told Reuters.
Call money deals, struck mostly at a steady 10.5 percent rate, accounted for half of the day's money market settlements.
Term rates were unchanged, with banks charging 14 percent for two-week, 15 percent for one-month and 18 percent for two-month money.
Insurers rolled over one-week funds at a flat 9.0 percent.
The central bank was active in the foreign exchange market today, buying 22 million marks and $2.0 million from commercial banks. It will inject kuna for this purchase on Thursday.
It calculated its kuna mid-rates for Wednesday weaker at 6.0603 to the dollar and steady at 3.5716 against the mark after the intervention. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
